rows.text: Mia’s 3, we’re in Vaughan. Swim, and anything nearby.

Three near you. Parent & tot swim, ages 2 - 4, Saturdays 9:15 a.m., off the town’s rec guide. Preschool playtime, ages 18 months - 4 years, drop-in, off the library’s page. Little movers, ages 2 - 5 — the community centre lists it, but the winter times aren’t posted yet. Want me to keep an eye on all of this for you? contrast.title: Without me
contrast.body: You set an alarm for 6:55 and open the tabs. Spots open at 7:00 a.m., and the good ones are gone by 7:02. Lose the $54 city session and private runs about twelve times that — and some towns give residents a head start of four days to two weeks.

Landing.seeBody: Four hours after the window opens I ask whether you got in. A few days after the first class I ask how it went. And in the evening, one line — how was today. Reply LESS and that becomes weekly, NO and it stops. What you tell me stays between us: no other family sees it, and the words themselves are gone in thirty days.

About.metaDescription: Hale is a planner for your kids’ year. Find what’s on. Hear how it went. Built by Anzhe Dong at Village Hale Technologies Inc. in Georgetown, Ontario.
About.lede: Once, a family had a village — elders who knew which class was worth it, neighbors who carried the small things, a grandmother who said this is normal, you are doing fine. That knowing hasn’t disappeared. It just has nowhere to live now except one parent’s memory — and no app fixes a memory problem by asking for more of your attention. So Hale is a number you text.
About.mission: Every parent should have someone who knows what’s on near them, remembers the date that fills in two minutes, and asks how it went. Across every stage of childhood, from the first months to almost grown.
About.howLede: Hale starts by telling you things and only ever does things with your say-so. The ladder is the whole product: it climbs one rung at a time, and only when you let it.

founderHeadline.text: Built by a parent, far from

About.founderStory: Hale is built by Anzhe Dong — a father, husband, and founder who spent years shipping production agentic systems. He started it raising a kid far from the village his own parents had: no elders down the street, no one who just knew which class was worth it. The trust was still out there, in what other parents told each other; it just couldn’t reach him. So he built the thing he kept wishing someone would text him.
About.cta: It starts with names, ages, and a postal code. No app, no account.

facts.title: What Hale asks for
facts.body: First names, ages, and a postal code. The first three characters are enough — they name a town, not a street.

facts.title: Nothing is sold
facts.body: A family’s information is never sold, never shared for advertising, and never shown to another family.

facts.title: STOP ends it
facts.body: A parent texts STOP and the messages stop. They can ask for their data, or for it to be deleted, at privacy@villagehale.com.

facts.title: A child’s words stay with their parent
facts.body: Hale talks to parents. For a child of 13 or older, a parent sees the topic and a summary rather than the words — unless there is a safety concern, and then the teen is told.

facts.title: Built and kept in Canada
facts.body: Village Hale Technologies Inc., Georgetown, Ontario. Family data stays in Canada, under PIPEDA and Quebec’s Law 25.

ForCentres.officialEyebrow: If a family asks whether Hale is official
ForCentres.officialLine: Hale is independent. It is not run by your centre, the town, the region, or the province. It checks every registration date against the town’s own page, and if the two ever disagree, the town’s page wins.

faq.question: Does a family need an account?
faq.answer: No. A parent texts a number and Hale replies. There is no app to install, no password, and no sign-up page.

faq.question: What does it cost a family?
faq.answer: Nothing to start. Watching the dates and answering questions is free, and families who join now keep the founding rate for good.

faq.question: Do we have to sign anything?
faq.answer: No. There is no agreement, and nothing for staff to report or track. The only thing we would set up with you is a poster carrying your centre’s code.

faq.question: What does Hale refuse to do?
faq.answer: It does not diagnose and it never names a dose — a medical question goes back to your care provider. It also never fills a registration form or holds a spot on a family’s behalf. It prepares and reminds; the parent registers.

items.question: What is Hale?
items.answer: A phone number your family texts. It finds what is actually running near your kids — swim, camps, drop-ins, the EarlyON down the road — watches the sign-up mornings where you live, hands you the town’s own link the night before, and comes back to ask how it went. It answers the parenting questions too, and does the admin once you say yes. There is no app to install and no account to create.

items.question: How do I start?
items.answer: You text the number and say hi. Hale asks for your kids’ names and ages and your postal code, and that is the whole setup — everything else it asks for later, only when it needs it. Hale never texts a number that hasn’t texted it first.

items.question: Does Hale do anything without asking?
items.answer: No. Hale drafts and you confirm — nothing reaches the outside world until you reply yes to that specific thing. Every message names exactly what was done, and Hale keeps the full record of who, what and when.

items.question: Is my family’s data private?
items.answer: Your data is stored in Canada and never leaves it, in line with PIPEDA and Quebec’s Law 25, and Hale never sells it. Every permission is granular and revocable in a text. Text messaging itself is not sealed the way an app is — a message crosses your carrier and Hale’s messaging provider — so Hale writes to that reality and names the task, never the diagnosis. A teenager’s content is redacted from parents by default.

items.question: Is this a bot? Who actually reads my texts?
items.answer: Hale is an AI assistant, and it never pretends otherwise. It is built and run by Village Hale Technologies Inc., a small parent-founded company in Georgetown, Ontario — and a real person reads anything you send to aloha@villagehale.com. Hale never texts a number that hasn’t texted it first, never asks you to text back a password, a card number or a code, and STOP ends the conversation at any time.

items.question: What does Hale actually watch?
items.answer: Municipal registration across 21 GTA municipalities — recreation programs, swim lessons, camps and after-school care — including the resident head start, the towns that register swimming on their own date, and the winter-break camps that open back in August. It also watches the waitlist clock, which is a day in some towns and two in others. And when the class you wanted is already full, Hale keeps watching it and texts you the minute a place opens.

items.question: How often will Hale text me?
items.answer: A heads-up the week a registration opens, the plan the evening before, and a nudge as it goes live. In the evening Hale asks one line about how the day went — reply LESS and that becomes weekly, NO and it stops. STOP works at any time.

items.question: Can Hale answer parenting questions, or only scheduling ones?
items.answer: Both. Ask about sleep, starting solids, potty training, picky eating, tantrums, screen time or routines and you get an answer pitched at your child’s age, plus the offer of the whole plan — two or three texts you can start tonight. A few days later Hale asks how it went. It never diagnoses and never names a dose.

items.question: Is Hale free?
items.answer: Hale is free while it is new, and families who start now keep their founding rate. A co-parent is always free — the same dates and nudges on their own number, never a second household to pay for.

items.question: Do I need to use the website?
items.answer: No. Everything happens in the text thread, and Hale will never send you to a website to finish a job you texted it to do. The full record of what Hale has done is yours whenever you want it — ask for it in the thread, or sign in with your phone number and read it there.

items.question: Will you tell me whether a class is any good?
items.answer: Not yet. Today Hale asks how it went. Telling the next parent what other families thought is what Hale wants to build next, and when it does it will be a count and a verdict — never anyone’s words.

items.question: Can you help when we travel?
items.answer: Not yet. Today I watch registration and what’s on where you live, in the GTA.

items.question: Can you tell me who else is going?
items.answer: Not yet. Today I only tell you about your own family, never anyone else’s.

items.question: Is Hale available outside Canada?
items.answer: Not yet. Hale is Canada-first because keeping your family’s data on Canadian soil is a core promise rather than a setting, and the registration data it watches is GTA municipal data. Other regions are on the roadmap.
